subject: Erase certification, backup-handling and georesidency playbook — follow-up
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@heliomed.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, HelioMed Legal <legal@heliomed.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliomed.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Evidence & timing for erase/residency — what you can commit to

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the DPA annex for the EU deployment, legal has two outstanding asks we need to close before the next steering committee:

- A concrete, auditable timeline for erasing customer data on primary and backup systems after a termination or erasure request (they want maximum windows for each tier).
- The type of evidence Redwood can provide that demonstrates erasure (audit log snapshots, signed attestation, certificate of destruction for on-prem transfers).
- Confirmation of whether backups are allowed to be held onshore in a Redwood-controlled region and whether those backups are covered by the same deletion window.

I've attached our standard evidence request (HelioMed_Evidence_Request_v2.pdf) with the specific fields legal needs. Can you confirm what you can commit to in writing (annex language or an attestation) and whether there's a workable schedule for a 30-day backup erase requirement?

We'd like to keep the DPA schedule tight, but open to a reasonable compromise if you can provide stronger attestation and log exports. Would you be available for a short follow-up on Wednesday?

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Security & Privacy
HelioMed

Attachment: HelioMed_Evidence_Request_v2.pdf (PDF, 185 KB)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@heliomed.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliomed.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T08:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence & timing for erase/residency — what you can commit to

Sofia — thanks for the clear list and for the doc. Quick summary of what Redwood can offer and one open dependency:

What we can commit to now (for inclusion in an annex):
- Primary data: logical deletion on the customer account within 7 days of a verified erasure request; soft-delete markers removed from primary serving stores and KV cache invalidated.
- Audit logs: we can provide an immutable audit log extract within 30 days showing the erasure job run and object counts.
- Attestation: signed attestation letter from Redwood’s CISO describing the erase operation and scope (we can provide a templated attestation for the annex).

Open question: backups and archival copies. Our standard practice is:
- Short-term snapshots (hot/warm) retained for rolling recovery are eligible for deletion within 30–45 days (depending on backup window).
- Long-term archival backups (cold store) may be retained longer for operational recovery and compliance; we can commit to an operational process to flag and wipe HelioMed-specific archives on request, but the timeline needs to account for cross-region replication and retention policies at the storage provider.

Proposal: If HelioMed requires a 30-day absolute maximum for all backup tiers, we can accept that with the following concessions to operational reality:
- Redwood will commit to initiating and completing deletion of all Redwood-managed copies within 45 days for backup tiers, and provide a certified attestation plus a log snapshot at 30 days showing deletion progress.
- For any data that is replicated to a HelioMed-managed sink (customer-controlled on-prem or self-managed bucket), eradication of those copies is HelioMed’s responsibility; Redwood will provide engineers and runbooks to assist.

I've attached a short playbook (redwood-erase-playbook.docx) that explains the steps, expected timelines, and the evidence artifacts we can export. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call Wed 10am UTC to finalize wording.

- Aisha
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-erase-playbook.docx (DOCX, 72 KB)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:04:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Evidence & timing for erase/residency — internal ask

Dev/Marissa — forwarding HelioMed's evidence request and my reply. TL;DR items we need to validate before the call:

1) Can we guarantee a signed attestation and an immutable audit-log export format (sha256-signed manifest) within 30 days of deletion? If yes, what team owns generation and signing and how long until we can operationalize a template?
2) Backups: is 45 days feasible for all Redwood-managed backups (including replicated snapshots), given we may rely on third-party storage lifecycle rules? We should write precise language: "Redwood will initiate and complete deletion within 45 days for Redwood-managed backups; attestation and log snapshot provided at 30 days."
3) For EU residency: confirm we can route deletion jobs to EU-hosted infra and record region-tagged artifacts (i.e., logs that show EU data-plane operations). Need a short checklist we can include in the annex.

Please reply inline so I can update the annex draft ahead of the Wed call.

Date: 2027-07-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Evidence & timing for erase/residency — what you can commit to

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@heliomed.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliomed.com>, HelioMed Legal <legal@heliomed.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence & timing for erase/residency — what you can commit to

Sofia — following our internal check and the Wed call, here is a proposed compromise and the concrete annex language we can sign: 

1) Timelines (annex wording):
- Primary data: logical deletion completed within 7 days of validated erasure request; audit log extract showing deletion run delivered within 7 days.
- Redwood-managed backups (hot/warm/cold): Redwood will initiate deletion for all Redwood-managed backup tiers within 30 days and complete deletion within 45 days.

2) Evidence & attestation:
- Redwood will provide a signed attestation (CISO) within 45 days certifying deletion completion.
- Redwood will deliver an immutable audit manifest (sha256-signed) within 30 days showing record ids and byte counts of deleted objects; a final audit export will be provided at 45 days.

3) Residency & onshore handling:
- Deletion jobs and supporting logs for HelioMed EU customers will be performed on EU-hosted infrastructure where available; log entries will contain an explicit region tag.
- If HelioMed elects to export data to a customer-managed on-prem sink, HelioMed will be responsible for purging those copies; Redwood will provide a technical runbook and in-engineer support to help verify that purge.

4) Certification for legal:
- We will deliver (a) the CISO attestation, (b) the 30-day audit manifest, and (c) the 45-day final audit export as evidence artifacts. We will also accept a clause that allows HelioMed to request an on-site or third-party verification if explicitly stated in the annex (costs/arrangements to be mutually agreed).

Next steps:
- I will upload an Annex A draft (DPA-Amendment-AnnexA-draft.docx) with the exact wording for the timelines and evidence deliverables and send a DocuSign link for signature. Link: https://app.docusign.com/HLMD/Amendment/12345
- If HelioMed can accept the 45-day final completion window for backups in exchange for the 30-day interim audit manifest and a signed attestation, Redwood will commit to the plan above.

Please confirm and we will generate the doc for signature.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): DPA-Amendment-AnnexA-draft.docx (DOCX, 28 KB); redwood-erase-playbook.docx (DOCX, 72 KB)
